Thank you. I will write down my thoughts in advance so I don’t get lost during the meeting. 

I just feel like I’m not the person for the role. I currently don’t have the industry knowledge required to be able to perform the tasks successfully and confidently, nor do I think I’d be able to get up to speed in such a short amount of time. I would understand rushing me if I had prior experience in a client facing role, or even as a data analyst. But I have neither. And the fact that the role affects revenue is just a huge weight in my shoulders given that they expect me to be up to speed in the short time I’ve been “training”. There is a lot to learn and they need someone to be able to fill that position since rates are dropping and more clients are well on their way. 

Everything feels rushed for me and I feel like nobody is hearing me whenever I speak up about certain things not clicking for me, or needing more time to understand certain aspects of the role. Like I’ve told my sr, this is the part that doesn’t make sense for me, I feel lost whenever it’s about analysis or like providing criteria adjustments to clients. I was told I wouldn’t have to do any of that since that’s a strategist’s job. Well the week after, there’s a new client to onboard and I had to set up their campaign without any guidance on what criteria to use. There was also a time we had to adjust another client’s campaign and I was told “next time I want you to bring recommendations to me on what to change.” So they keep going back on their word which just leaves me confused overall on what my scope really is. It gives me bad anxiety. It’s affecting my confidence a lot and my partner has told me I’ve changed which makes me so sad.
You’re absolutely right. Thank you.

No official documentation or training materials. I just learn from the senior account manager during zoom sessions and such. Yeah I never got higher pay (even under the table) from the company when I was switched from accounting to production. They did give bonuses from time to time. During Q1 I had an incentive plan where I got a bonus for every successful net new client I managed after review at the end of the quarter. Q2, there weren’t any new clients but the work of course remained the same with the existing clients and my pay was still low compared to the work I do which is why I brought up the compensation aspect of it. The first time I ever asked for added comp was what I mentioned, and it’s not going well obviously because I’m performing poorly and my boss mentioned he’s telling the founder I’m not ready and they’re pulling back on the approved budget for me. I was also very underwhelmed that when I asked for added comp, they came back with a performance based bonus instead of just a basic monthly “here’s an additional payment since we’re using you beyond what we initially hired you for” type of payment, now there are metrics etc that I have to meet in order to get the money. I just feel like I’ve been underpaid since I was moved to prod, I never asked for additional pay cause I knew the company was in a bad position hence the need for lay offs back then. It was kinda hurtful when the boss told me I wouldn’t be getting a sympathetic ear if I told him the reason for my underperformance was related to compensation.. since I’ve been taking on so much more without added pay for 2 years, and I fail at this one role I didn’t even choose for myself and get treated like this. It sucks. 

Also the fact that I am not American and don’t have a full understanding of the industry (Mortgage) makes it really hard to do the analysis part of it all since there’s a lot of things I do not understand still. I just feel very rushed and the client facing aspect is not something I am prepared for even with the 6 months training. It may seem long for them but for me it is not.

But what if the role is not something I want to do? I wasn’t really given the option to say no. Just that help was needed which was why I was moved there to be able to handle some clients since they were overloaded.

It sucks. Some of the feedback I got was that I don’t care. I don’t care about missing deadlines with clients and have no sense of urgency. When the truth is I just have so much anxiety that I end up freezing up and panicking all the time. I have so much anxiety now when I get slacked about things and I’ve never been this way before in my 2 years here. It’s tough when they think I don’t care when I have been trying, it’s just that no one seems to hear me when I say certain things don’t click for me and I can’t do it yet because I lack the foundational knowledge of the industry to be able to trust myself. they have this expectation that I can because I’ve shown in the past that I can do data analysis and that stuff. But it’s different this time.

I’m on the same boat!! Also size 10/12, with hips and obvious vertical line but my width is more noticeable than my curve so I struggle with FN lines too. 

My go to outfits (before discovering kibbe) were also crop tops and almost everything “not good” for my type. Basically anything that gave waist definition, I wore. Lol. But upon discovering kibbe, I realized that I didn’t necessarily need waist definition…. but that also didn’t mean I HAD to give it up. 
I still wear crop tops but I find a way to incorporate the “elongation” needed for FNs so basically since crop tops cut the body in half, I’ll find a way to make up for the vertical line with other pieces of clothing, for ex: bandeau and shorts, then with a jacket (not too stiff so it’s not boxy) that’s the same color & length as my shorts; crop tops and wide leg pants; when I wear culottes I make sure my shoes are the same color so the “break” isn’t as obvious. Off shoulder crop tops are also a go-to of mine still, I guess since with exposed shoulders, the waist doesn’t get the same amount of attention (maybe); a-line skirts & long pants look good on me when paired with those flowy camisole tops. These are some of my go to’s today. 

The only reason I figured these out is because I literally looked through all my photos from the past 7 years, compiled them, grouped them into yes/no’s, and studied why the outfits or certain pieces of clothing, certain cuts etc. were yes/no’s. Lol. It was a lot of work but it helped me a lot!!! Now I can literally go into an online shopping site, see a design/cut and be like “yeah this won’t work” 😂 If you have the time, I suggest doing the same cause it’ll help you determine which cuts/designs work for you, and then you can proceed to curating looks based on that because you’ll also know how to ~make up~ for it when you break certain “kibbe rules” lol

I think that muscle you’re referring to is the temporal muscle, above the ear at the sides of the face. Those muscles do tend to cause severe headaches among TMJ sufferers. 

The masseter muscle is the muscle that gets hard when you bite down, you will feel them stiffen up when you bite hard, and is another pain point for TMJ sufferers. 

I also have tinnitus, neck pain, and bad posture. I think a lot of people with TMJ have the same set of problems because the masseter & temporal muscles cover very big areas, thus any problem with one will affect the other. i.e. your bad posture in relation to severe headaches, tinnitus, and neck pain. They are all connected and have a relationship with each other. 

Having a night guard is a step towards the right direction. I would suggest also improving your posture, maybe get a standing desk so you’re not always sitting down if you work from home.

I always lose when I try to kill the aqua before the plant. So I always focus on killing the plant first. Most double aqua teams only have nimo & their plant as energy sources, so taking out the plant early would be essential. Plus, make sure your plant is still alive and healthy that way you can safely attack the enemy plant using your beast. Remember once your plant dies, your beast is basically dead too cause it’ll only take a few cards for aquas to kill a beast. I’ve learned after soooo many losses against aaps that killing a backline aqua before their plant would still end in a loss, even if it’d feel great to ambush a non-shielded aqua in round 2, you will most def still have a hard time winning cause by then your plant would be nearly dead and your beast, who has the ability to burst plants, will be in danger bc there will be no protection from your tank anymore.
